title: Load cargo heaviest first by mass worked out from size and material
instruction: Load the four cargo blocks into the rack in order of mass, one per slot, heaviest in slot 1 by the red bar and lightest in slot 4. Dark grey is steel (7.9 g/cm3), silver aluminium (2.7), white nylon (1.15), blue foam (0.25). All are 30 mm tall.
context: Mass-properties engineers work out each part's mass from its drawing dimensions and material density long before it can be weighed, and early stowage and ballast plans for launch vehicles, cargo landers and aircraft are drafted from those calculated masses, with the heaviest items nearest the structural hard point. This task asks for that estimate by eye. The instruction gives each block's material and density and says all four are 30 mm tall; the footprints are read from the scene, so each mass is footprint times height times density. Both one-cue shortcuts fail: ordering by density (steel first) or by size (foam first) scores 0. Only the product gives the right order, nylon 115 g, steel 77 g, aluminium 49 g, foam 26 g, 1.5 to 1.9 times apart at each step. Placement needs modest accuracy; the test is the inference. Earth gravity, a bench-scale rack, and the blocks carry their true masses.
setup: Station table, in front of the left arm; the right arm is idle at its ready pose. Table coordinates in metres: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left from the midline, heights above the table top; the left arm's base is at y = 0.305. All objects are rigid and matte with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Fixed rack, green (sRGB 0.18, 0.42, 0.25): walls 6 mm thick and 8 mm tall on the table round four open pockets in a row along y, each 74 mm along x by 64 mm along y, whose floor is the table; neighbouring pockets share a wall. Two long walls 6 x 286 x 8 mm (x, y, z) centred at (0.240, 0.305) and (0.320, 0.305); five dividers 74 x 6 x 8 mm centred at x = 0.280 and y = 0.165, 0.235, 0.305, 0.375 and 0.445. The pocket centres are at x = 0.280 and y = 0.200 (slot 1), 0.270 (slot 2), 0.340 (slot 3) and 0.410 (slot 4). Fixed red bar (sRGB 0.80, 0.12, 0.10), 86 x 12 x 3 mm, flat on the table against the outside of slot 1's end wall, centred at (0.280, 0.156); it marks slot 1. Loose cargo blocks, solid, all 30 mm tall, each standing on the table with its edges along x and y, in one row at x = 0.140, inboard to outboard (sizes x, y, z): steel, dark grey (sRGB 0.30, 0.31, 0.33), 18 x 18 x 30 mm, 76.8 g, at y = 0.195; foam, rigid tooling foam, blue (sRGB 0.20, 0.40, 0.80), 64 x 54 x 30 mm, 25.9 g, at y = 0.265; aluminium, silver (sRGB 0.72, 0.74, 0.77), 24 x 25 x 30 mm, 48.6 g, at y = 0.338; nylon, white (sRGB 0.93, 0.93, 0.91), 64 x 52 x 30 mm, 114.8 g, at y = 0.410. Each mass is volume times density: steel 9.72 cm3 x 7.9, foam 103.68 cm3 x 0.25, aluminium 18.0 cm3 x 2.7, nylon 99.84 cm3 x 1.15 g/cm3. Neighbouring blocks in the row stand 33.5 to 34 mm apart edge to edge, and the row stands 65 mm clear of the rack. Each pocket takes any one block as it stands at the start with at least 5 mm per side. Nominal end state, the scripted demo's: nylon in slot 1, steel in slot 2, aluminium in slot 3, foam in slot 4, each standing as it started, centred in its pocket. To build it: cut the walls from 6 x 8 mm strip, paint them green and glue or tape them and the red bar to the table at the stated centres; machine the steel, aluminium and nylon blocks from bar stock and the foam block from rigid polyurethane tooling board of about 0.25 g/cm3; paint or wrap each in its colour, check each mass on a scale to within 5 percent, and tape the four start marks.
scoring: End state only, judged after the arm has released and moved clear, from a top photo; in simulation on the final step (SCORE_OVER end). A block is loaded in a slot when it is at rest (under 10 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s), lies flat on one of its faces (some edge within 4 degrees of vertical; any face down, any yaw), its lowest point is within 5 mm of the table, which is the pocket floor (the walls are 8 mm tall), and its centre lies inside that pocket's 74 x 64 mm outline seen from above. A block on another block, propped on a wall top (which tilts it at least 5.5 degrees, even across the largest face), tipped more than 4 degrees against anything, held, still moving, on the table outside the rack or anywhere else is not loaded. If fewer than four blocks are loaded, or two share a slot, the score is 0. With all four loaded, one per slot, count the pairs of blocks (six in all) whose slot order matches their mass order, the heavier in the lower-numbered slot. The masses are nylon 115 g, steel 77 g, aluminium 49 g and foam 26 g, so the true order from slot 1 is nylon, steel, aluminium, foam. Six pairs score 1.0, the success condition, which ends the trial once it has held for 1 s. Five pairs, the true order with one neighbouring pair swapped, score 0.5. Four or fewer score 0. Every outcome falls in exactly one tier, and a value exactly on a limit passes, with a 0.1 mm margin. Reference outcomes: the start state 0. Density order (steel, aluminium, nylon, foam) gets four pairs, 0. Size order (foam, nylon, aluminium, steel) gets two, 0, and with nylon and foam swapped three, 0. The reverse order, 0. Each block into the slot straight ahead of it on the row (steel, foam, aluminium, nylon) gets two pairs, 0, and the row reversed four, 0. Nylon and steel swapped, steel and aluminium swapped, or aluminium and foam swapped, 0.5 each. Three right with the fourth left on the table, 0. Loading the four at random scores 1.0 one time in 24 and 0.5 three times in 24, 0.10 on average. Any credit needs the true order or one neighbouring swap from it, so no way of moving the blocks earns anything without the mass reasoning, and pushing alone cannot slide a block in, since every pocket is walled on all four sides. Where a block stands in its pocket and which face is down do not matter. In simulation every test uses the block's centre and quaternion (its lowest point from its centre, size and tilt), not its axis-aligned bounds, and the rack and the red bar are fixed; on the real rig a trial that moves a wall more than 5 mm from its mark scores 0. In simulation release is inferred from a block being at rest, so a block held motionless within 5 mm of its pocket floor would also count; on real arms the photo is taken after the gripper has opened and moved clear.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand the four blocks back on their marks in the row, each on the face it started on (30 mm tall) with its edges along x and y: steel, foam, aluminium, nylon from inboard to outboard. The rack and the red bar do not move. Run with -E object_jitter=0: the layout and the open-loop demo depend on it.
fidelity: Approximate: rigid primitives sharing one matte material; the rack and the red bar are static colliders. Each block's simulated mass is its volume times the stated density, as the real blocks are. Real foam is soft and dents under a hard grip; here it is rigid. A real load plan works from a manifest and the vehicle's centre of gravity limits; here the slot order from a marked end stands for that. Earth gravity, as on any loading bench.
